title: news24: does a strong high-volume candle continue when it coincides with a burst of relevant news, compared with the same candle without news?
motivation: Operator hypothesis 2026-10-08: when a strong candle with a volume spike coincides with a burst of relevant news, the move continues for more than 2-3 bars. Candle-only tests (lean21, wave23, xvol9, xvol10, daytype14) averaged all big moves and found chance. The hypothesis is that news-backed moves continue and moves without news revert, so the average hides both. Issue: https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/310
before_registration: No outcome of this test computed. Computed before this file: GDELT file sizes from masterfilelist.txt; event candidate counts per instrument/TF/window (price and volume only, count.py); GKG theme names in one sample file (themes_probe.py); per-file relevant-row counts of the first ~70 fetched GKG files (no link to prices). Self-checks on synthetic data only.
declared: Development evidence only. 2019-2022 and 2023+ have both been inspected by earlier campaigns for other questions. 2023+ is a development window, not a holdout. No test ledger, nothing qualified, nothing shipped.

feasibility.source: GDELT 2.0 GKG 15-minute files (V1 Themes, V1 Locations, V1 Organizations, V1 Persons, DocumentIdentifier)
feasibility.sizes_2019_on: GKG 1541 GB compressed in ~268k files; Events export 22.4 GB (no themes); Mentions 35.2 GB (no themes). DOC 2.0 API gives 15-min timelines only for spans <= 1 day (hourly for 1 week) and rate-limits at ~1 request per 5-20 s, so ~17k requests (~2-4 days) for 6 instruments.
feasibility.choice: GKG, streamed and filtered in memory, fetched only for (a) a 4-hourly baseline grid (file timestamps 00,04,08,12,16,20 UTC, from 2018-12-01) and (b) the two files each event candidate needs. ~39.7k files, ~200 GB transferred, ~15 h serial at ~1.4 s per file (0.5 s polite delay, md5 checked, resume-safe via news24.db). Filtered store: per-file totals and per-instrument counts plus the matched rows (truncated URL and themes), estimated ~9 GB, below the 30 GB cap.
feasibility.rejected: Full GKG download (~1.5 TB, ~5-7 days serial); Events export (no themes, ~90 h serial for the full series); BigQuery (bills a GCP project, needs operator consent).

relevance: relevance.json (frozen by its hash below): an article is relevant to an instrument if any rule matches (GKG themes, organizations, persons, URL substrings, optional country filter on V1 Locations).
lookahead_guard: A GDELT file may be used for a bar only if its file timestamp is <= the bar's close time (bar start + TF). The two news windows of an event are the newest file with timestamp <= close (e1 = floor(close / 15 min)) and the file before it (e1 - 15 min). All baseline grid files are strictly older than e1 - 15 min. Asserted in news24.news_features; boundary fixture in news24.selfcheck. Caveat: GDELT publishes a file a few minutes after its timestamp, so live availability lags this rule by a few minutes.

event.price: |mid close - mid open| >= 1.5 x production ATR14 (entry TF) of the previous bar; side = sign of the body
event.volume: z of log(1 + tick volume) vs the same UTC slot over the prior 20 non-weekend observations (>= 10), weekend bars (Fri 21:00 - Sun 22:00 UTC) excluded; z >= 2.0
event.cooldown: next event of the same instrument/TF >= 60 min after the previous qualifying bar
event.spread_rule: ask close - bid close at the signal bar <= 0.2 R (R = 1.5 x ATR14 at the signal bar); filtered events are dropped

news_burst.measure: share = relevant rows / all rows, summed over the two news windows
news_burst.baseline: single-file shares of the 4-hourly grid files in the 14 days before the older window, >= 40 files; z = (share - mean) / sd
news_burst.NEWS: z >= 2.0 AND >= 5 relevant articles in the two windows
news_burst.no_data: either news window missing or the baseline has < 40 files: excluded from both groups, counted

outcome.entry: open of the bar after the event bar, in the event direction; long at the ask, short at the bid (labels_v2.simulate, fills.resolve)
outcome.management: harness stop definition: R = 1.5 x ATR14 at the signal bar, stop -1 R, stop to breakeven-plus-costs after +1 R (one-bar latency), target +3 R, time exit at the close of bar H; the opposite-supertrend-flip exit is disabled (pure continuation test)
outcome.metrics: mean net R (bid/ask), continuation rate = share of net R > 0, mid gross move over 6 bars (diagnostic)

windows.w2023: 2023-01-01 .. newest data (development window, not a holdout)

stats: moving-block bootstrap over trading days (validate.day_boot; day = 22:00 UTC roll), block 5, 1000 reps, seed 24, 95% percentile CI; NEWS - CONTROL from the same day draws
primary_metric: mean net R NEWS - CONTROL at H = 6, WTICO/USD M5

decision_rule.PASS: WTICO/USD M5 H6: NEWS mean net R CI lower bound > 0 in BOTH dev and w2023, AND NEWS - CONTROL CI lower bound > 0 in BOTH windows
decision_rule.LEAD: not PASS, but NEWS - CONTROL CI lower bound > 0 in at least one window for WTICO/USD M5 H6, or the same PASS pattern in another instrument (secondary, no multiplicity correction, needs its own registration)
decision_rule.small_n: a cell with fewer than 30 NEWS events is flagged as underpowered

secondary: the other 5 instruments, M1 and M15, H3 and H12: reported, never decision-eligible
